articles.title: Three ways to connect a WhatsApp number to Bitrix24 (and what each one costs you)
articles.excerpt: If your customers write to you on WhatsApp, sooner or later someone asks the same question: "Can we see these chats inside Bitrix24?" The answer is yes, but there is more than one way to do it, and th…
articles.body: If your customers write to you on WhatsApp, sooner or later someone asks the same question: "Can we see these chats inside Bitrix24?" The answer is yes, but there is more than one way to do it, and the differences matter more than most vendor pages admit. This article walks through the three common approaches, what you give up with each, and how to decide. Why connect WhatsApp to a CRM at all A WhatsApp number that lives on one manager's phone has three problems. Only one person sees the conversation. The history leaves with the phone, or with the employee. And nobody can measure response time, because nothing is recorded anywhere a manager can audit. Bitrix24 already has a place for customer conversations: Open Channels (Open Lines).
articles.author: TehProf.kz

articles.title: Where an agent's tokens go: 9 real GitHub bugs, two Gemini Flash-Lite models, 1 fix each
articles.excerpt: I gave two Gemini Flash-Lite models the same 9 real bug reports from GitHub and let each one work in a loop: search, read a file, edit, run the tests, submit. Each model fixed one bug. Between them th…
articles.body: I gave two Gemini Flash-Lite models the same 9 real bug reports from GitHub and let each one work in a loop: search, read a file, edit, run the tests, submit. Each model fixed one bug. Between them they made 964 model calls. The tasks come from SWE-bench-Live (github.com/microsoft/SWE-bench-Live, MIT). I picked small pure-Python repos I could run on a Windows machine without Docker: attrs, faker and cfn-lint. A task only counts if the original tests fail before the fix and pass with the real fix applied. The agent never sees the new tests. When it submits, I apply them and run them. If they fail, it gets one more attempt and sees the tail of the failing output, like a CI log. Each attempt is capped at 30 steps.

articles.title: ChatGPT Reads the Lyrics, Not the Tune
articles.excerpt: When you talk to ChatGPT it feels like it is listening. I wanted to know what actually arrives on the other side, so I picked the simplest thing a voice carries besides words: a melody. I hummed Happy…
articles.body: When you talk to ChatGPT it feels like it is listening. I wanted to know what actually arrives on the other side, so I picked the simplest thing a voice carries besides words: a melody. I hummed Happy Birthday to ChatGPT, in every way the app lets me speak to it, and then ran the same question at scale through the voice models OpenAI sells to developers. Two buttons, two different things The microphone and the voice button do not do the same job. The small microphone is Dictation: OpenAI's help page describes it as turning a recording into editable text, which you then send like anything you typed. The other button opens Voice, a spoken conversation that today runs on a model called GPT-Live-1.1. With Dictation the model only ever sees text, and a hum has no text.

articles.title: You Don't Need That useEffect: Derived State in React
articles.excerpt: A search box over a list. It works, and it shows up in code review every week: function Results({ items, query }) { const [filtered, setFiltered] = useState(items); useEffect(() => { setFiltered(items…
articles.body: A search box over a list. It works, and it shows up in code review every week: function Results ( { items , query } ) { const [ filtered , setFiltered ] = useState ( items ) ; useEffect ( ( ) => { setFiltered ( items . filter ( ( item ) => item . name . includes ( query ) ) ) ; } , [ items , query ] ) ; return < List items = { filtered } /> ; } Type a letter and the list updates. Nothing looks broken. But every keystroke renders Results twice, and the first render shows the old list. The mental model: a copy that runs late If you can calculate it from props or state, it isn't state. Calculate it while rendering. filtered is a copy of an answer you already have. items and query are the source.

articles.title: The Fix That Brought the Bug Back
articles.excerpt: I use a second iPhone at home through a stream (the setup): the phone's screen comes off USB as H.264, an old laptop's GPU re-encodes it, and a fork of Sunshine streams it to my main phone. The bug in…
articles.body: I use a second iPhone at home through a stream ( the setup ): the phone's screen comes off USB as H.264, an old laptop's GPU re-encodes it, and a fork of Sunshine streams it to my main phone. The bug in this post appeared twice. The second time, my fix for the first one was the cause. Round one: nothing for ten seconds Connecting to the phone was slow. Sometimes the picture took a couple of seconds; sometimes the client gave up after ten: Connection started Connection terminated: -100 (ten seconds later: no video traffic) Reconnecting usually worked at once. The same client connecting to a Mac running Sunshine never did this. The difference is where the picture comes from. Sunshine on a Mac captures the screen itself, so it has a picture the moment you connect.

articles.excerpt: Building a Polymarket Grafana Dashboard: Monitoring P&L, Latency, and Execution Health Your Polymarket bot is running. The process is alive, WebSocket connections appear healthy, and orders are being…
articles.body: Building a Polymarket Grafana Dashboard: Monitoring P&L, Latency, and Execution Health Your Polymarket bot is running. The process is alive, WebSocket connections appear healthy, and orders are being submitted. But are those orders filling? Is the bot losing money after fees? Is market data arriving late? Has a rejected order caused the internal position tracker to drift away from the exchange? A green process-status indicator cannot answer those questions. A Polymarket Grafana dashboard should make the difference between software that is running and a trading system that is operating correctly immediately visible.

articles.title: Interaction Nets Explained: The Programming Model Behind the Frostbite CPU
articles.excerpt: On November 18, 2026, the chip-design startup Architect Labs published a post introducing Frostbite. They describe it as a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set. They say their AI systems des…
articles.body: On November 18, 2026, the chip-design startup Architect Labs published a post introducing Frostbite . They describe it as a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set. They say their AI systems designed it, from the compiler down to the final chip layout. The Hacker News thread reached 657 points and 342 comments. Most coverage is about the AI and the headline number: 4.59x better performance per watt than a conventional core. This article looks at the part software developers can try today. Frostbite runs programs as interaction nets , a model of computation that is more than 35 years old. The language that compiles to it, Vine, is open source, and you can install it with Cargo today. A note on sources: I have not run Vine or seen Frostbite hardware.

articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 21 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Voyager’s Neptune Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet . Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton , and faint system of rings.
